## Why the disabled workflows are disabled

The repository holds no record of why any `disabled_manually` workflow is disabled. For each one, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `changelog.d/`, `.vibey-gh.toml` and the scripts' TOML files were searched for its name beside any of disable, pause, switched off, turned off, suspend; `git log --all` was searched for those words in commit messages and for each workflow's name in `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `.vibey-gh.toml` (`-S`). Every hit was the workflow's creation or a feature change, with two exceptions that are not the answer:

- #1809, #1813 and #1505 pause the backlog killer through `[backlog_killer] enabled` in `scripts/daily_lanes.toml`. That is a different switch from the GitHub-side `disabled_manually` state, and it does not name the splitter or any other workflow.
- ADR-0072 (the Sabbath window) describes held work as paused, which is a code-level guard, not a disablement record.

So the "why disabled" for every row is `unknown, operator to say`. Nothing here infers a reason. One bounded fact the data does give: each disabled workflow's newest run is dated in the Last run column, so it was disabled after that date (the API reports no disable timestamp).

## Caveats

- The window includes runs of workflows that were later disabled; their run counts are before the disablement. The active and disabled estimates are shown apart for that reason.
- Job minutes come from the newest runs per workflow, so they follow whatever those runs happened to be (a cancelled or in-progress run contributes the minutes it had). The window estimate scales the sample mean to the run count; treat it as an order of magnitude.
- `updated_at` is the run's last update and can postdate completion after a re-run, so wall time can read long; it also includes time waiting for a runner. Queueing is therefore inside the wall figure, not separated from it.
- Runs with no jobs in the API are counted as zero minutes and noted per workflow in the JSON (`runs_without_jobs`); jobs with no start or end are counted in `jobs_without_timing`.
- An empty `billable` object in the run timing API is recorded as no data, not as 0 ms; the cost block says which it was.
- The billed-dollar figure covers only the probed runs named in the cost block. Jobs in the `other` runner bucket (a self-hosted label, or no label) are outside it, and a runner OS with no probe recorded was not probed, whether because the sample held no completed run on it or because its timing read failed. If the cost block names a self-hosted label, that disagrees with the repository's note that every CI workflow runs on GitHub-hosted runners only; this document does not decide which is right, the operator is to say.
- Workflows with `event` `dynamic` (Dependabot, Copilot, dependency graph) are GitHub-run, not defined in `.github/workflows`.

## Reproduce

`uv run python scripts/ci_cost_baseline.py collect` writes a NEW stamped record under `docs/architecture/evidence/` (settings in `scripts/ci_cost_baseline.toml`: repository, window days, sample size, output pattern) and refuses to overwrite an existing file unless `--force` is given. It makes only `gh api` GET calls. Exit status: 0 clean, 2 written with unknowns (listed on stderr), 1 nothing written. To point the document at a new record, set `baseline` in the TOML and run `render`; `check` exits 1 when the document and the record disagree.
